fields.sample_size: 300 households targeted, 270 responded (strata: peri-urban 68.1%, mountainous 29.2%, coastal/island 2.7%; island/coastal under-sampled because of time-limited data collection); 14 in-depth interviews with technical officers and managers; precision level 7%
fields.effect_estimate: Rural piped water access in Quang Ninh is 56.6% (urban 73.85%; Vietnam rural 55%); island and coastal areas have the lowest centralised supply rate (48.16%) while using piped water was highest there (57.7%) among respondents; improvements are largest in peri-urban areas that connect to urban systems, with disparities in mountainous and island areas and treatment-technology constraints at several centralised facilities. The authors conclude that governance capacity (technical management and the supporting framework), more than infrastructure availability, is the primary determinant of sustainability; no statistical test of this claim is reported. Descriptive.
fields.study_design: mixed-methods case study (household questionnaire survey and in-depth interviews, one province)
fields.section: Full text: Methodology 3 (site, sampling, precision 7%); Results 4 (access by stratum, facility management); Conclusions
fields.exact_location: Methodology 3 (site, sampling, precision 7%); Results 4 (access by stratum, facility management); Conclusions

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a household survey (270 households) and 14 interviews in Quang Ninh Province, Vietnam, read in full text 2026-10-04. Peri-urban improvement, mountain and island disparities; governance capacity argued to matter more than infrastructure (descriptive, not tested).

notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds strata shares and access percentages. Peri-urban-dominated sample (68.1%) limits generalisation to mountain and island areas. MMAT rating left in place.
